theory.intro: Integrating the acceleration vector componentwise gives velocity, and integrating again gives position. Each integration adds a **vector constant** $\underset{\sim}{c}$, not a single number. Fix the two constants using the given initial velocity and initial position.
facts: Integrate the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ component and the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ component separately.
The constant of integration is a vector $\underset{\sim}{c}=c_{1}\underset{\sim}{i}+c_{2}\underset{\sim}{j}$, so each component gets its own constant.
Substituting the initial velocity into the general velocity gives both components of the first constant.
Substituting the initial position into the general position gives both components of the second constant.
Find the velocity constant before integrating a second time, or the position will be wrong.
An initial condition may be given at a time other than $t=0$; substitute that time instead.
Check the answer by differentiating it twice and by substituting the given conditions.
steps: Integrate each component of $\underset{\sim}{a}(t)$ and add a vector constant
Use the initial velocity to find that constant, giving $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
Integrate each component of $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$ and add a second vector constant
Use the initial position to find that constant, giving $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$

A particle has acceleration $\underset{\sim}{a}(t)=-\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j}$, with $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=3\underset{\sim}{i}+4\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=2\underset{\sim}{i}-\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find $\underset{\sim}{r}(3)$.

development.question_text: A particle has acceleration $\underset{\sim}{a}(t)=\sin t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+\cos t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=3\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$.

A particle has acceleration $\underset{\sim}{a}(t)=4e^{2t}\underset{\sim}{i}-6\underset{\sim}{j}$, with $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=3\underset{\sim}{i}+5\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=\underset{\sim}{i}$. Find $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.

mastery.question_text: A particle has acceleration $\underset{\sim}{a}(t)=6t\,\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}$ and position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{3}+5t-2)\underset{\sim}{i}+(9t-2t^{2}+1)\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find the initial velocity and the initial position, and verify that they are consistent with the given acceleration.

A particle has acceleration $\underset{\sim}{a}(t)=-10\underset{\sim}{j}$, with $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=18\underset{\sim}{i}+30\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=\underset{\sim}{0}$. Find the position vector of the particle at the instant it next returns to the level $y=0$.
mastery.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=18\underset{\sim}{i}+(30-10t)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$
$=18t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(30t-5t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$
$30t-5t^{2}=0$
$5t(6-t)=0$
$t=0$ or $t=6$
The particle starts at $t=0$, so it returns when $t=6$.
$\underset{\sim}{r}(6)$
$=108\underset{\sim}{i}+(180-180)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=108\underset{\sim}{i}$

\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$}, xmin=-12, xmax=126, ymin=-8, ymax=56, xtick={54,108}, ytick={45}, width=12cm, height=8cm, samples=100, clip=false]
\addplot[thick, domain=0:108] {5*x/3 - 5*x*x/324} node[pos=0.78, above right] {$y=\frac{5x}{3}-\frac{5x^{2}}{324}$};
\addplot[only marks, mark=*, mark size=1.6pt] coordinates {(0,0) (108,0)};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
